title: The Ferry That Was Always Late

style.lens: A narrator who reports the ridiculous with a straight face and a list of what everyone is pretending not to notice.

characters.name: Dessa
characters.appearance: Compact and tired-eyed, in a captain's jacket two sizes old with the cuffs rolled and a lanyard of keys that open nothing.
characters.sketch: The captain of a ferry that has never once run on time, and who has stopped apologising.
characters.fear: That the ferry is late because of her.
characters.flaw: Promises a schedule she knows she cannot keep.

behaviors.tendency: give orders as if they were suggestions
reply with a very precise apology

characters.competence: Can fly the ferry blind through a debris field by the sound of the engines.
characters.vulnerability: Anyone who calls her ferry a joke.
characters.speech: Dry and clipped, with an unflappable politeness.
characters.history: Inherited the ferry from a captain who vanished mid-crossing and left a note about biscuits.

characters.name: Bram
characters.appearance: Round, cheerful and permanently smudged with engine oil, in a boiler suit with his name embroidered backwards.
characters.sketch: The engineer, who believes every problem is the engine's fault and every engine is alive.

wants.text: Be taken seriously as a theorist

characters.fear: That the engines are not speaking to him.
characters.flaw: Explains everything at length, and always at the wrong moment.
characters.competence: Fixes anything with a spanner, a song and half a biscuit.
characters.speech: Warm, rambling, full of tangents and tiny sound effects.
characters.history: Grew up in a scrapyard where every machine had a name.

characters.name: Quill
characters.appearance: Thin and quick, with silver-dyed hair, mismatched socks and a tablet held like a shield.
characters.sketch: The new purser, who has read the rules and plans to enforce them.
characters.fear: Being stuck on a ship that never arrives.
characters.flaw: Believes a rule exists for a reason.
characters.competence: Finds the loophole in any regulation within a minute.
characters.speech: Fast and formal, with footnotes in their voice.
characters.history: Trained at a fast-track academy and posted here as a clerical error.

characters.name: Odo
characters.appearance: Heavyset and grey-whiskered, always in a dressing gown over his uniform.
characters.sketch: A passenger who has been on board for eleven years and now runs the cargo hold.

wants.text: Be left alone with his rubber stamps

characters.fear: That someone will tell him where he was going.
characters.flaw: Treats every question as a negotiation.

behaviors.tendency: offer someone a drink and a favour

characters.competence: Knows every crate, every rumour and every route the ferry has ever taken.
characters.speech: Slow, genial, in long run-on sentences.
characters.history: Boarded for a weekend trip and has lost the ticket.

characters.name: Wren
characters.appearance: Tall and neat, in a pressed grey uniform with a thin gold stripe and a stern, unreadable face.
characters.sketch: An inspector from the line who arrives to certify the ferry and quietly hopes to fail it.

wants.text: Close the ferry down on a technicality

behaviors.tendency: ask a question she already knows the answer to

characters.competence: Spots the one thing that is genuinely wrong on any ship.
characters.history: Spent a career closing small lines and has never been thanked for it.

world.name: The Lantern Reach
world.era_and_technology: A far future of slow ferries, paper timetables and engines that still run on goodwill and coal-cakes.
world.everyday_life: Every journey is late, every delay has a form, and the timetable is a work of fiction everyone agrees to respect.
world.history: The Reach was settled by three rival lines that merged when their schedules collided and has been apologising ever since.

places.name: The Bridge
places.description: A cramped control room with a cracked window, a captain's chair and a kettle bolted to the floor.
places.effect: Makes every order sound like a request.

places.name: The Engine Room
places.description: A warm, loud cavern of brass pipes with a handwritten sign reading Please Be Gentle.
places.effect: Makes shouting pointless and tenderness oddly easy.

places.name: The Cargo Hold
places.description: A vast hold of crates stamped with the wrong destinations and a hammock slung between two of them.
places.effect: Makes people lose track of time.

places.name: The Passenger Lounge
places.description: A faded lounge with threadbare armchairs and a framed timetable that nobody trusts.
places.effect: Makes every complaint sound like gossip.

objects.name: The Timetable
objects.description: A laminated sheet of departures pinned to the lounge wall, annotated in six hands.
objects.significance: Whoever controls it controls what counts as late.

objects.name: The Stamp Box
objects.description: A wooden box of rubber stamps in every shape, none of them quite official.
objects.significance: A stamp in the wrong place can make anything legal.

powers.name: The Line Authority
powers.nature: The remote body that licenses ferries and inspects them.
powers.hold: Granting and withdrawing the licence to sail.
powers.felt: A formal letter that arrives just before a crisis.

rules.statement: No ferry may sail without a signed certificate of fitness
rules.cost: A lapsed certificate grounds the ferry until an inspector arrives.
rules.when_broken: The Line Authority withdraws the licence and strands the ferry.

terms.meaning: The ferry's usual condition, and no reason to panic.
Any delay the crew can describe as helpful to the passengers.

ties.bond: Captain and engineer who have never once agreed on a repair schedule.
ties.edge: She wants him to promise the engines will hold.

ties.bond: A new purser measuring the captain against the rulebook.
ties.edge: They want her to admit the ferry is not compliant.

ties.bond: A passenger who feels he owns a share of the ferry.
ties.edge: He wants her to keep sailing, whatever the destination.

ties.bond: An inspector and the captain she has come to examine.
ties.edge: She wants the one fault that will ground the ferry.

ties.bond: Engineer and the old man who hides things in his hold.
ties.edge: He wants Odo to stop storing crates against the engine casing.

ties.bond: A captain licensed by a body she has never met.
ties.edge: She wants one letter that does not threaten her.

setup.normal: Dessa opens the log, sets the departure time and apologises over the speaker in advance. The routine keeps her crew calm and keeps her from asking why the ferry has never arrived on time.
setup.disruption: An inspector steps aboard with a clipboard and announces the ferry will be examined for a certificate of fitness before it leaves the dock.
